artworks.title: Acrisius Orders Danaë and Perseus into the Chest (Attic calyx-krater, after the Triptolemos Painter)
artworks.year: first half of the 5th century BC
artworks.description: Side B of the Hermitage calyx-krater (ARV² 360.1): King Acrisius commands that Danaë and the infant Perseus be shut in the chest — the Argive oracle made into Attic red-figure before the sea takes them.

artworks.title: Danaë and the Infant Perseus Cast Out to Sea by Acrisius
artworks.description: Ghisi's engraving (Metropolitan Museum of Art) stages the exile: Acrisius sets his daughter and grandson into the vessel that will float to Seriphos — the grandfather's fear made into a Mannerist print.

artworks.title: Danaë and Perseus Set in a Boat
artworks.artist: Battista Angolo del Moro (after Giorgio Ghisi)
artworks.description: A Rijksmuseum etching after Ghisi's design repeats the same Argive sentence: Acrisius consigns Danaë and Perseus to the water, hoping to outrun the discus that will still find him at Larissa.

popCulture.title: Acrisius
popCulture.description: The Argive king who locked Danae in bronze and cast her to sea — the grandfather Perseus' discus was fated to kill.

popCulture.title: Danaë
popCulture.description: Acrisius' daughter and the shower of gold — her imprisonment is the father's fear that made Perseus' birth inevitable.

popCulture.title: Clash of the Titans
popCulture.creator: Desmond Davis
popCulture.description: Harryhausen's film keeps Acrisius' oracle and the chest at sea as the opening move of Perseus' quest.
